  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Excluding `)` from `_COMMENT_WORD_STARTS` means a `#` immediately after a closing subshell group is not stripped as a comment, so `$(...)` inside the comment is detected as an active command substitution and changes the command family.
  WHY: This misclassifies commands such as `(cd /tmp)# $(date)` into a separate `subst` family; all reviewers rate the edge case NIT, with no severity disagreement.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `file_patterns`, lines 912–942 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Family lookup and issue creation are not coordinated across invocations.
  WHY: Concurrent sessions with different command shapes in the same new family can each create an issue after reading an index with no issue for that family.

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:362 (`_COMMENT_WORD_STARTS = " \t\n;&|("`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Removing `)` correctly handles `X=$(pwd)#suffix`, but also means a `#` after a closing subshell group is not recognized as a comment start.
  WHY: For `(echo x) # $(date)`, `_strip_shell_comments` retains the commented substitution and `_has_command_substitution` can classify it as active, routing the report to a different family.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: 362 (`_COMMENT_WORD_STARTS = " \t\n;&|("`); 518-547 (`_has_command_substitution`); 553-576 (`_strip_shell_comments`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Removing `)` to handle `X=$(pwd)#suffix` prevents the comment stripper from recognizing a `#` immediately after a closing `)` of a subshell or command grouping.
  WHY: `(cd x && git status)#$(date)` retains the comment and detects `$(date)`, adding `subst` to the family; the whitespace variant `(cd x && git status) # $(date)` does not. The reviewer describes this as a known tradeoff and notes that the inverse case is not tested.

  PROBLEM: The comment scanners exclude `)` as a character that can start a comment.
  WHY: After a shell group closes, an adjacent `#` starts a comment. In `echo ok; (true)# $(date)`, the scanners retain and detect `$(date)`, adding the `subst` family construct.

  PROBLEM: Family lookup and issue creation are not coordinated across invocations.
  WHY: Concurrent stage sessions with different command shapes in the same new family can both read an index with no issue for that family, then each POST a new issue. The in-memory registration only coordinates patterns within one invocation.
